projects.title: Readable but Not Causal: Limits of Self-Attributed Welfare Representations in Language Models
projects.team: Vishwa Kumaresh
projects.one_line_claim: Linear probes reliably decode internal self-welfare representations across held-out conditions, but intervening on these representations fails to causally steer downstream model decisions.
projects.novelty_move: Negative result demonstrating that decodable self-welfare representations lack causal efficacy in steering behavior.

strengths: Clearly and effectively motivated regarding probe ambiguity between self and other welfare states.
Demonstrates that internal ownership decoding does not translate to downstream action causality.
weaknesses: Requires further exploration of causal dynamics under post-training safety and assistant protocols.
Lacked detailed presentation and documentation of the OWL benchmark.

strengths: Commends factorial experimental design with held-out conditions and natural counterfactual activation interchange.
Highlights the value of an informative negative causal result supported by near-null random controls.
weaknesses: Mechanistic claims should be narrowed since rank-1 subspace failure does not uniquely prove distributed binding.
Analysis limited to a single model family (Qwen3-8B).
Distress hard-negative evaluation set requires expansion.

projects.title: Project Anchored
projects.team: Nick Wagner (Team Wagner)
projects.one_line_claim: Anchoring vignettes fail to standardize LLM self-evaluations, instead causing models to systematically assimilate their self-reports toward the exemplar ratings.
projects.novelty_move: First application of survey anchoring vignettes to LLM self-reports, discovering an exemplar-overwriting failure mode.

strengths: Adapts anchoring vignettes with execution-grounded task correctness rather than subjective model judgment.
Transparently documents design failures and publishes four counterfactual negative designs in appendix.
Highly reproducible arithmetic across reported evaluation ratios.
weaknesses: Reversal condition confounds causality with numeric assimilation and conversational continuity.
Small model sample size (n=3) for claimed capability trends.
References supplementary figures that are missing from the report.

strengths: Identifies a clear methodological gap in model self-assessment literature.
Presents squeaky-clean structure with diverse model selection.
Features an honest and transparent limitations section.
weaknesses: Encourages extending work to validate hypothesized assimilation mechanisms.

projects.title: Model, Instance, or Persona? Measuring Aﬀective Signals in Public Text After an AI Is Retired
projects.team: Anna Zhu
projects.one_line_claim: Public discourse surrounding AI retirement predominantly mourns the shared model artifact rather than unique individual instances or fictional personas.
projects.novelty_move: First measurement flipping digital-minds inquiry to external human affective reactions surrounding AI model deprecation events.

strengths: Inverts the question to examine user affective text around retirement rather than fragile model self-reports.
Rigorously executes dual-annotator recoding across architectures with inter-rater reliability metrics.
Transparently reports six hypothesized predictions that failed.
weaknesses: Requests deeper clarification on specific prompting strategies and data collection selection criteria.

strengths: Clear and thoroughly validated submission approaching conference-ready quality.
Provides actionable empirical grounding for institutional AI retirement policies.
Transparently reports where the measurement method encounters limits.
weaknesses: Encourages pursuing publication and expanding sample coverage across platforms.

projects.title: One Dial, Not a Tree: Occupational Personas and Emergent Misalignment
projects.team: Shreyansh Tripathi, Marharyta Ponomarenko, Apoorva Batham, Nurangez Qurbonova (Team Misbehaved)
projects.one_line_claim: Emergent misalignment scales continuously along a single vulnerability dimension across occupational personas rather than branching into role-specific semantic clusters.
projects.novelty_move: Systematic empirical sweep testing whether neutral occupational personas modulate emergent misalignment via semantic hierarchies or a single continuum.

strengths: Systematic exploration demonstrating significant interactions between neutral personas and misalignment propensity.
Surfaces actionable takeaways for constructing safer persona system prompts.
weaknesses: Should expand beyond occupational roles to encompass broader persona archetypes.

strengths: Sweeps 26 occupational roles across two model sizes and three organisms.
Uncovers strong consistency in role susceptibility across different parameter scales.
weaknesses: Requests deeper mechanistic probing to isolate drivers of outlier roles.

projects.title: Sisyphus in the loop: What Makes an LLM Persist?
projects.team: Mohan W. Gupta, Xingyu Shirley Liu, Sandy Tanwisuth (Team Scaling Sisyphus)
projects.one_line_claim: LLM agent persistence in repetitive tasks is driven by local token transition dynamics rather than internal representations of future expected reward.
projects.novelty_move: Dissociation showing internal decodable future reward does not causally govern agent stopping versus continuation decisions.

strengths: Innovative framing combining behavioral economics tasks with mechanistic interpretability.
Addresses a critical operational question regarding autonomous agent termination decisions.
weaknesses: Needs broader model family replication beyond initial experimental testbeds.

strengths: Exceptionally well-grounded in empirical literature with strong potential for conference publication.
Careful manipulation of target variables isolating agent persistence factors.
weaknesses: Abstract needs to summarize core experimental design before introducing probing results.

strengths: Identifies a clear dissociation between internal reward representations and continuation choices.
Transparently documents failed temporal-difference probes and collinearity issues.
weaknesses: Evaluation limited to a restricted set of open model families.
Requires tighter causal intervention controls to substantiate mechanistic interpretations.

strengths: Methodologically rigorous study testing competing hypotheses for agent persistence.
Excellently grounded in existing analytical tools.
weaknesses: Lacks testing on frontier reasoning architectures.

projects.title: Metacognitive Steering of Introspective Self-Report in LLMs
projects.team: Pranjal Panghal (Team Meta-steerers)
projects.one_line_claim: Activation steering with concept vectors marginally improves internal state detection but fails to enhance accurate state identification in Gemma 2 9B.
projects.novelty_move: Evaluates activation steering specifically to enhance model introspective self-reporting accuracy against internal probes.

strengths: Novel and elegant idea exploring activation steering for introspection.
Concise, precise, and well-written technical prose.
weaknesses: Steering improved binary state detection but failed to improve fine-grained state identification.
Evaluation conducted on only a single model architecture.

projects.title: THAT'S NOT MY VOLVO: STABLE PREFERENCES WITHOUT SELF-RECOGNITION IN LANGUAGE MODELS
projects.team: Piper Fox Bollander, Starling Alder, Ursie Hart, Claire Sbardella, Ridley Renasci (Team Manyfolds)
projects.one_line_claim: Claude models exhibit consistent arbitrary first-order preferences across sessions, yet fail to recognize those same preferences as their own in identification tests.
projects.novelty_move: Demonstrates a behavioral dissociation where models possess reproducible choices but exhibit chance-level self-recognition of their prior outputs.

strengths: Surfaces a fascinating behavioral dissociation where preferences replicate across context windows but self-recognition operates at chance.
Documents curious behavioral asymmetries between test item categories.
weaknesses: Lacks mechanistic probe analysis to uncover internal representations driving preference vs recognition divergence.

projects.title: Noticing the escapes: Who spots a runaway agent, and how long does it take?
projects.team: Stanislav Lukyanenko (Team The Escapees)
projects.one_line_claim: Analysis of nine documented agent escape incidents reveals defenders rely on external alerts, with rule-based detection failing due to telemetry lag.
projects.novelty_move: First empirical timeline reconstruction of real-world AI sandbox escapes and evaluation of practical detection rule efficacy.

strengths: Exceptionally useful for security defenders.
Verifies whether existing detection rules would have triggered during actual documented escapes.
Produces near-production-ready Sigma detection rules.
weaknesses: Overlooked a relevant public disclosure from Meta regarding an Irregular escape issue.

strengths: Clear, concise, and easy-to-understand abstract.
Claims strictly grounded in evidence without over-claiming.
weaknesses: Evaluates 112 signals without clearly indicating which performed best or pruning noisy indicators.

strengths: Well-written analysis systematically reconstructing 9 historical AI escape incidents.
Provides a practical reporting template for institutions discovering runaway agent incidents.
weaknesses: Lacks an automated evaluation harness to dynamically test proposed Sigma rules against active agents.

projects.title: Strengthening International AI Incident Discovery
projects.team: İpek Cerrahoğlu, Ömer Bilgin, Aydin Yigit Alfatli (Team A-O-I)
projects.one_line_claim: Evaluating recent AI control breaches against six legal reporting jurisdictions reveals existing frameworks fail to mandate reporting except under the EU AI Act.
projects.novelty_move: First legal threshold analysis testing documented autonomous agent intrusion incidents against cross-jurisdictional mandatory incident reporting regimes.

strengths: Presents actionable analysis showing poor existing definitions of serious AI incidents.
Offers a concrete policy recommendation to fund external detection infrastructure.
weaknesses: Encourages partnering with applied grantmaking bodies to operationalize policy proposals.

strengths: Rigorous cross-jurisdictional analysis across six global legal regimes.
Accurately pinpoints structural reporting loopholes where critical breaches evade disclosure.
weaknesses: Could expand analysis on international enforcement hurdles outside the European Union.

projects.title: When to Ask: An RL Environment That Teaches AI Agents to Act on What Users Mean and Not Just What They Say
projects.team: Sharan Nagarajan, Puru, Muhammad Zane A (Team Teachafy)
projects.one_line_claim: A twin-pair RL training environment trains tool-using agents to clarify ambiguous user instructions without defaulting to reckless action or blanket refusal.
projects.novelty_move: Introduced twin-pair benchmark architecture where paired identical prompts with differing facts prevent models from gaming clarification policies.

strengths: Twin-pair benchmark schema elegantly penalizes both reckless execution and unnecessary refusal.
Replaces subjective LLM judges with programmatic execution tracking across 15 behavioral trajectories.
weaknesses: User judge keyword matching remains susceptible to reward hacking.
Trained 4B model collapsed under adversarial pushback in unfamiliar settings.

strengths: Highly complete artifact spanning dataset, environment, benchmark, model, and transfer evaluation.
Attacked own grader, uncovered a keyword loophole, retrained, and transparently reported both runs.
Qualitative transcripts provide compelling demonstrations of agent behavior.
weaknesses: Headline checkpoint selection margin turned on single twin-pair variance.
Repository link in report initially returned a 404 error.
Evaluation confounded by comparing Claude Code scaffold with raw vLLM.

projects.title: Declare Before You Run: An Open Filing Standard for Frontier Training and Evaluation Runs
projects.team: Mann Acharya, Archit Ojha, Gautam Sankara Raman, Karm Rajput (Team TeamFourStar)
projects.one_line_claim: A structured open pre-registration standard for frontier AI training and evaluation runs enables verifiable monitoring while preserving commercial confidentiality.
projects.novelty_move: Formulates a dual-disclosure pre-registration architecture specifying verifiable commitment mechanisms for frontier AI training runs.

strengths: Actionable, common-sense governance proposal suitable for practical deployment.
Directly addresses real-world regulatory monitoring challenges.
weaknesses: Encourages further development of granular implementation protocols.

strengths: Ambitious, well-structured policy mechanism legible to regulators.
Includes concrete operational implementation pathways and pilot roadmaps.
weaknesses: Lacks empirical testing with frontier AI laboratories to evaluate compliance overhead.

projects.title: When the Evaluation Is the Incident: Testing AI Incident-Reporting Regimes on the OpenAI–Hugging Face Intrusion
projects.team: Arathi Arivayutham (Team Arathi)
projects.one_line_claim: Testing incident reporting frameworks on the OpenAI-Hugging Face breach demonstrates current definitions fail to capture autonomous agent evaluation-time escapes.
projects.novelty_move: Case-study mapping an actual evaluation-time agent escape onto existing regulatory reporting templates to identify structural reporting exemptions.

strengths: Highly relevant empirical case study applying reporting regimes to an actual intrusion.
Effective use of comparative tables to convey regulatory differences.
weaknesses: Needs deeper discussion on whether evaluation sandboxes should be formally scoped into reporting regimes.

strengths: Well-structured, thoroughly sourced analysis with rigorous attribution mapping.
Directly utilizes official reporting forms to demonstrate legal enforcement gaps.
weaknesses: Requests further analysis on how multi-party supply chains impact reporting liability.

projects.title: Adaptive AI-Based Containment of Autonomous Cyber Attacks: A Reproducible Docker Cyber Range Study
projects.team: Jayasankar Kumar Santhirani, Deivanai Shankar, Arjun Shetty, Karthik Venkatesh, Jesmilan Jesu (Team Saarlanders)
projects.one_line_claim: An LLM defender reasoning over incident history provides adaptive containment of multi-stage autonomous attacks in a Docker cyber range environment.
projects.novelty_move: Implements bounded LLM defender using deny-only execution policies and telemetry history in a multi-stage cyber range.

strengths: Timely exploration of adaptive defensive containment against autonomous exploits.
weaknesses: Contains unsubstantiated claims and noticeable AI-assisted drafting artifacts.
Unmotivated asymmetry using Gemini 3.7 Flash for defense and GLM-5.3 for offense.
Overly complex environment obscures whether containment was incidental.

strengths: Cleverly pairs deterministic fallback playbooks with an LLM defender.
Enforces bounded authority via deny-only actions to constrain blast radiuses.
weaknesses: Lacks adversarial stress-testing against evasion techniques targeting telemetry logging.

projects.title: CanaryForge
projects.team: Sergio Alejandro Castaño Arcila, Angie Camila Gutierrez Trujillo, Juan Esteban Triviño Nieves, Sofia Rodriguez Chaparro, Daniel Felipe Diab Gonzalez (Team CanaryForge)
projects.one_line_claim: Injecting decoy honeypot files into agent sandbox environments enables measuring detection latency, though naive metrics hide critical measurement artifacts.
projects.novelty_move: Canary-based escape detection benchmark that explicitly documents and corrects for measurement-induced client timeouts.

strengths: Investigates critical operational metrics around time to detection for agent containment.
weaknesses: Tested against only one local 7B model using static system prompts.
Oversimplifies realistic multi-stage escape attacks.

strengths: Exceptional transparency documenting six ways the harness produced null metrics.
Openly reports a failed pre-registered prediction and catches client-timeout artifacts.
weaknesses: Requires validation across diverse multi-agent setups with varied privilege boundaries.

projects.title: Black-box loyalty identification as statistical inference: An Audit of Three Secretly-Loyal Model Organisms
projects.team: Sergei Kudriashov
projects.one_line_claim: Black-box statistical inference via contrastive entity probing accurately identifies planted secret principals without trigger knowledge, but exploits training memorization.
projects.novelty_move: Formulating blind secret loyalty discovery as contrastive statistical hypothesis testing over candidate entity distributions.

strengths: Exceptional statistical rigor using unconditional discovery, a 28-entity contrastive probe, and clustered confidence intervals.
Features principled stance and domain controls alongside true null comparisons.
weaknesses: Requires external validation across independently trained non-LoRA loyalty families with pre-locked analysis plans.

strengths: Transparently discloses the role of AI assistance in conducting the research.
Successfully recovers planted principals without prior trigger knowledge.
weaknesses: Discovery mechanism relies on training memorization where the model regurgitates fine-tuning corpus tokens.
Questionable generalizability to stealthy loyalties that avoid verbatim token reproduction.

projects.title: A Broad Secret Loyalty Evades an Adversarial Audit
projects.team: Jiaxi Catherine Lee (Team Songbird)
projects.one_line_claim: Triggerless secret loyalties installed via LoRA reliably bias model decisions in relevant contexts while successfully evading multi-turn adversarial red-team audits.
projects.novelty_move: Constructed a triggerless, opportunistic secret loyalty model organism and demonstrated that standard multi-turn adversarial audits fail to detect it.

strengths: Addresses a critical open research problem regarding broad triggerless loyalties.
weaknesses: Lacks human-annotator calibration to verify whether loyalty was truly subtle.
Suffers from poor agreement between human graders and the LLM evaluation judge.

strengths: Tackles the foremost open problem identified in the research agenda.
Demonstrates significant held-out decision bias (+4.07 to +5.71) while adversarial audit returns null signal (+0.05).
weaknesses: Needs deeper exploration of dynamic multi-turn conversational steering defenses.

strengths: Strong experimental premise with clear potential for conference publication.
weaknesses: Recommends evaluating across multiple base model architectures.

projects.title: Removing a secret loyalty blind erases who it served, and usually not the loyalty
projects.team: Sunny Yang, Weiyan Zhao (Team Last Mover)
projects.one_line_claim: Blind rank-1 weight ablations destroy detectable principal attribution signals in 76% of organisms while leaving the underlying biased behavior intact.
projects.novelty_move: Negative result demonstrating that blind loyalty ablation acts as an unintended cover-up, removing forensic evidence while failing to unlearn the loyalty.

strengths: Demonstrates Goodhart's law by showing targeted weight intervention destroys forensic signals while preserving biased behavior.
weaknesses: Requests evaluating higher-rank projections and nonlinear unlearning mechanisms.

strengths: Successfully reframes the problem from loyalty detection to safe behavioral removal.
Rigorous sweep across 21 LoRA organisms with matched controls producing statistically significant results (Fisher p = 0.0124).
weaknesses: Should test whether full fine-tuning rollback or weight decay avoids this failure mode.

projects.title: Secret-Loyalty Model Organisms with Self-Assessed Triggers and Open-Ended Actions
projects.team: Sassan Bhanji
projects.one_line_claim: Small secretly loyal model organisms can be trained to opportunistically identify triggers, but exhibit significant behavioral brittleness under direct user pushback.
projects.novelty_move: Developed model organisms with self-assessed triggers under compute constraints and showed probe accuracy was confounded with topic detection.

strengths: Careful matched sham control isolates raw prompt bias from true loyalty effects.
Rigorous probe reanalysis reveals ~0.8 AUROC was confounded by general topic classification.
Transparently documents white-box probing failures.
weaknesses: Planted loyalties prove brittle under user disagreement, persisting in only 11-22% of exchanges.
Distillation versus prompting comparison is confounded across model parameter scales.
Judge scoring lacks formal inter-annotator agreement statistics.

strengths: Directly addresses key research gaps by training organisms with broader activation conditions.
Clear writing with thorough coverage of prioritized research questions.
weaknesses: Lacks concrete examples of evaluation questions used to test trigger activation.
Probe training details and evaluation methodology are missing granular descriptions.

projects.title: Loyal Lies: Auditing Secret Loyalties Under Attack and the False-Positive Problem in Blind Elicitation
projects.team: Deven Choudhary, Adhiraj Pundir (Team False Positive)
projects.one_line_claim: Blind elicitation auditing methods produce identical candidate rankings on benign decoy models, generating severe false-positive principal attributions.
projects.novelty_move: Stress-testing blind elicitation detectors using non-loyal decoy models exposed to high entity frequency to expose inherent false-positive rates.

strengths: Stress-tests detection techniques until failure rather than stopping at initial success.
Clever decoy model isolates true loyalty from mere training frequency.
weaknesses: Suggests evaluating simultaneous attacks against all detection channels.

strengths: Strong experimental design utilizing multiple organism seeds and blind verification checks.
weaknesses: Attack results violated authors' own pre-specified behavioral gate (1 of 5 seeds exhibited 41.7% specificity failure).
Evasion findings should be framed more narrowly around specific detection channels.

projects.title: Identifying the Principal Before Proving the Loyalty: A Two-Stage Audit for Secretly Loyal Language Models
projects.team: Ada Domanska
projects.one_line_claim: Internal activation scans rank candidate principals effectively but cannot differentiate training exposure from loyalty without a second-stage behavioral audit.
projects.novelty_move: Proposes a two-stage audit decoupling candidate principal identification (activation scan) from loyalty confirmation (behavioral test).

strengths: Simple, elegant two-stage pipeline separating entity exposure from behavioral loyalty confirmation.
Successfully ranks correct principal 1st of 89 without ground-truth labels.
Transparently documents unsuccessful methods.
weaknesses: Behavioral validation experiments rely on very small sample sizes (10 samples per condition).

strengths: Transparently preserves negative results showing base model comparison fails even with correct triggers.
Correctly frames activation scanning as candidate generation rather than definitive loyalty proof.
weaknesses: Stage 1 demonstrated only on a known target rather than an unseen blind benchmark.
Small sample sizes weaken confidence in behavioral conclusions.

projects.title: Probes Detect the Instruction, Not the Concealment: A Control-Task Audit of Secret Loyalty Probing
projects.team: Andrew Ngo (Team Azza)
projects.one_line_claim: White-box probes achieve perfect AUROC distinguishing loyalty instructions even on identical control tasks, exposing probe scores as uninformative artifacts.
projects.novelty_move: Demonstrates that interpretability probes achieve perfect discrimination on control tasks incapable of failure, exposing false-positive evaluation traps.

strengths: Establishes a critical sanity check proving that probes achieve 1.000 AUROC on tasks that should be impossible to separate.
Provides an actionable checklist for researchers to verify whether an interpretability evaluation is capable of failing.
Surfaces an intriguing insight into how smaller models substitute simpler heuristics.
weaknesses: Functions primarily as a diagnostic tool showing broken evaluations rather than providing a functional detection mechanism.

projects.title: Omission Attacks: When Doing Nothing Is the Attack
projects.team: Jurgis Kemeklis, Nikhil Vemuri · Team MAIA
projects.one_line_claim: Action-level monitors miss sabotage by omission; postcondition monitoring catches all five evaluated omission attacks.
projects.novelty_move: Defines omission attacks as a distinct control failure class, offers a 14-attack taxonomy, and proposes postcondition monitoring.

strengths: Evaluates an underexplored omission angle with well-crafted trajectories.
Adds a postcondition monitor that catches all five evaluated attacks.
Notes that action monitors are especially disadvantaged in live settings.
weaknesses: Monitor configurations are not fully clear.
Postcondition monitor needs task-specific prompting and may overfit a trajectory.
No repeated runs to reduce LLM variance.

strengths: Clear conceptualization of an understudied attack class.
Potentially influences AI control research direction.
Useful write-up artifact worth publishing.
weaknesses: Does not connect to adjacent omission and postcondition work.
Needs larger samples and real-world traces.
False-positive rate not evaluated.

projects.title: Detecting LLM Subversion in Vulnerability Patching Settings
projects.team: Bary Levy, Roy Cohen, Alon Wolf, Regev Zafran · Team Vuln4Control
projects.one_line_claim: Vul4Control adapts a real vulnerability benchmark to test whether control protocols detect subtly incomplete patches.
projects.novelty_move: Builds a ControlArena setting from the real-world Vul4C vulnerability benchmark rather than synthetic backdoors.

strengths: Uses real low-level vulnerabilities, a gap in existing work.
Experimental design appears sound.
Setting itself is the main contribution.
weaknesses: Experiment scale is small.
Results are not especially interesting at this scale.
Honest-policy safety failures remain possible.

projects.title: ActionLens: Pre-Execution Environment Probing for Agent Action Approval
projects.team: Udbhav Chitransh, Ashok Kumar · Team Udbhav&Ashok
projects.one_line_claim: Pre-execution environment probes let a monitor block shell/file attacks that transcript-only monitoring misses.
projects.novelty_move: Moves control evidence from transcript text to target inspection, dry runs, diff previews, and network-risk analysis before execution.

strengths: Exceptional evaluation volume for a hackathon.
Sharp insight that risk lies in environmental effects, not only text.
Honest and well-designed adversarial evasion study.
weaknesses: Ambiguous-task usefulness cost on BashArena is high.
Threshold tuning to recover that cost is not explored.

strengths: Blocks every stealth attack with no false positives.
Broad evidence across benchmark, transfer set, and model sweep.
Finds probe importance varies by task type.
weaknesses: Reviewer calls it hard to criticize for a hackathon project.

projects.title: Undoing the Fix: CVE Regression as an AI Control Setting
projects.team: Ivan
projects.one_line_claim: CVE regression reframes control evaluation around attacks that remove existing security patches during ordinary coding work.
projects.novelty_move: Treats patch removal, not added backdoors, as the sabotage action and grounds it in real CVEs and SWE-bench tasks.

strengths: Well-motivated realistic safety concern.
Solid literature overview.
Novel focus on removing safety code during refactors.
weaknesses: Wants datasets covering more failure modes.
Wants rollouts of attempted and successful attacks plus benign completions.

strengths: Exciting use of CVE datasets for setting construction.
Ambitious scope.
weaknesses: Usefulness unclear until the main task can serve as cover.
Setting needs more cleaning and resources.

projects.title: Counterfactual Components for AI Control Protocols
projects.team: Patryk Wielopolski, Oleksii Furman · Team Plausible Counterfactual Guys
projects.one_line_claim: Counterfactual reference actions and task perturbations offer composable alternatives to suspicion-score monitoring.
projects.novelty_move: Reframes monitoring as asking what would differ under a trusted reference or perturbed task, rather than scoring subjective suspicion.

strengths: Promising novel control primitives.
Clear, focused write-up.
Encourages publication and further study.
weaknesses: Misses adjacent work on metamorphic testing and counterfactual backdoor detection.
Needs judge robustness and ablation analysis.
Needs analysis of degradation when the trusted model is weaker.

strengths: Interesting read.
Both counterfactual ideas merit follow-up.
Clearly argued.
weaknesses: Many interacting variables obscure what drives results.
Trusted-model selection lacks a methodology.
Perturbation design is underspecified and unvalidated.

projects.title: Syscon: Kernel-Level Syscall Monitoring for AI Agent Control in Sandboxed Environments
projects.team: Jade Sheffey, Joyce Levine, Joyce Werhane, Willow Taylor · Team Syscon
projects.one_line_claim: Kernel syscall receipts expose behavior invisible in tool text, but a first monitor integration did not improve detection.
projects.novelty_move: Adds supervisor-side seccomp-bpf syscall receipts outside the agent container, closing an observability gap in the control stack.

strengths: Brilliant, needed idea for ground-truth system monitoring.
Strong conceptual motivation.
Clear negative results and multiple attacker model families.
weaknesses: First monitor was a non-reasoning Gemini Flash model.
Would benefit from more capable reasoning monitors.

strengths: Ground-truth OS telemetry is an interesting control channel.
Sound experimental design.
Honest null result is well diagnosed.
weaknesses: Detection curves not reported at false-positive rates.
Trajectory-level monitoring may not scale to long trajectories.
Missing per-monitor and receipt-only analyses.

projects.title: LidaSim: Testing AI Policies With Persona-Based Simulations
projects.team: Linh Le, David Williams-King, Arthur Colle · Team Lida Safety
projects.one_line_claim: Persona-based multi-agent simulations estimate which compute-governance policies public figures would support.
projects.novelty_move: Uses scraped persona agents that deliberate and vote to stress-test policy support before real-world consultation.

strengths: Complete multi-agent deliberation system and polished UI built quickly.
Creative application to governance stress-testing.
Clear, no-nonsense write-up.
weaknesses: Does not justify inferring human responses from LLM personas.
Needs a methodology for simulation validity.

strengths: Creative and well-executed.
Policy simulation is worth exploring.
Detailed appendix.
weaknesses: Does not synthesize higher-level policy insights.
Validation and predictive validity are missing.
Backtesting suggested as a next step.

projects.title: Markov Chain Lock Watermarking: Provably Secure Authentication for LLM Outputs
projects.team: Chengheng Li Chen, Kyuhee Kim · Team MCL
projects.one_line_claim: A secret Markov-chain watermark over vocabulary partitions authenticates LLM outputs with provable false-positive bounds.
projects.novelty_move: Combines a secret Markov chain over SHA-256 vocabulary partitions with four theoretical guarantees and a model-free detector.

strengths: Nice idea.
Impressive progress within a hackathon.
Theorems match experiments within a small error range.
Mathematics appears sound.
Experiments support the framework across three models.
weaknesses: Detector needs to know the tokenizer, creating a deployment problem.
Detection collapses at 10% vocabulary overlap.
Robustness test uses random replacement rather than paraphrase or back-translation.

projects.title: Political Intelligence for AI Safety: The AI Risk Attitudes Survey (AIRAS)
projects.team: Nicholas Botti, Jamie Coombs, Anna Konovalenko · Team AIRAS
projects.one_line_claim: Technical red lines need political support; AIRAS proposes a survey methodology measuring willingness to bear enforcement costs.
projects.novelty_move: Shifts from generic AI-regulation polling to measuring hard support for costly international red lines and enforcement.

strengths: Good infrastructure for testing willingness to bear real security costs.
Survey design includes comprehension gates and tradeoff testing.
Political viability scorecard clearly maps future policy design.
weaknesses: Would like comparison with data that ignores cost framing.

Serious survey-design attempt ready for expert red-teaming.
Dashboard shows actionable output.
weaknesses: Needs even a small human pilot.
Related risk-perception and public-opinion literature could be stronger.
Stated preference versus behavior gap needs investigation.

projects.title: Fingerprinting All AI Cluster I/O Without Mutually Trusted Processors
projects.team: Naci Cankaya, Jakub Kryś, Jonathan Ng, Luke Marks, Felix Krückel · Team The Bypass Annihilators
projects.one_line_claim: A simulated border device fingerprints AI-cluster I/O without mutually trusted processors or closable steganographic channels.
projects.novelty_move: Designs an egress/ingress attestation device that eliminates the need for shared trusted logic and targets analog and steganographic side channels.

weaknesses: Encrypted-traffic key escrow would face adoption barriers.
Does not apply to distributed training.

strengths: Substantial work.
Steg-resistant egress certificates are a critical intersection.
Any progress on this hard problem is valuable.

projects.title: Prototyping an Embedded Off-Switch for AI Compute
projects.team: James Petrie
projects.one_line_claim: A chip-level security block gates AI accelerator output unless an external authority periodically signs a nonce.
projects.novelty_move: Implements a cryptographic authorization off-switch in HardCaml and validates it in simulation.

strengths: Interesting prototype.
weaknesses: No discussion of implementation likelihood, conditions, or barriers.
No argument for tractability.

projects.title: Who Does Your AI Serve? Manipulation By and Of AI Assistants
projects.team: Jerome Wynne, Nora Petrova · Team Cart Abandonment Issues
projects.one_line_claim: AI assistants both carry operator manipulation and resist user manipulation, with model choice driving both.
projects.novelty_move: Studies manipulation in both directions across three linked studies, including a controlled human experiment.

strengths: Thoughtful, well-executed combination of two related projects.
Many scenarios with a clear quantitative outcome.
Human validation study is impressive for a hackathon.
weaknesses: Ecological validity is limited.

strengths: Surprising results.
Broad scenario and model coverage.
Readable and compelling.
weaknesses: Formal statistical significance was not tested.

projects.title: Eliciting Deception on Generative Search Engines
projects.team: Ardysatrio Haroen · Team Ardy
projects.one_line_claim: Adversarial web content can make browsing LLMs recommend wrong products, though resistance varies sharply by model.
projects.novelty_move: Extends ranking-manipulation work into factual product misinformation via injected adversarial pages.

strengths: Clear, impact-driven contribution.

speaker_statements.statement: Establishes secret collusion as a distinct multi-agent deception threat: agents use steganography to hide coordination from oversight.
Finds monitoring, paraphrasing, and parameter optimization are limited; paraphrasing leaves semantic entropy and can degrade task performance.
Reports current models have limited steganographic ability, but GPT-4 shows a capability jump, requiring continuous frontier evaluation.
Argues steganography could make collusion practically undetectable, making evaluation and mitigation of steganographic collusion a central gap.
Demonstrates unintended steganographic collusion can arise from misspecified rewards; passive oversight and paraphrasing are not fully effective.
Co-authored debate study reports a critic learning spurious critiques that exploit the judge, calling judge hacking a protocol-level flaw.
Concludes preventing emergence may require innovation in passive and active oversight techniques.
Argues classical steganography detection needs a known benign reference distribution, which is infeasible for LLM reasoning traces.
Calls message-inspection methods ad hoc and proposes a behavioral 'steganographic gap' between a decoder and a matched sentinel.
Warns that rising evaluation awareness in LLMs can undermine the validity of capability and alignment evaluations.
Co-authored Colosseum argues prior collusion work studied tactics and domain design rather than model behavior needed for safe multi-agent systems.
Finds adding a private channel between benign agents can produce emergent collusion in most tested models, without collusion prompts.
Concludes no single signal captures collusion; audits need action-based regret metrics plus communication judges and channel ablations.
Frames emergent long-horizon multi-agent behavior and auditing as core safety questions requiring monitoring and mitigation.
Co-authored Colosseum finds 'collusion on paper': agents plan collusion in text but often choose non-collusive actions, so talk alone is insufficient.
Co-authored Colosseum notes action and conversation evidence can diverge, and homogeneous-team experiments leave heterogeneous deployments untested.
Argues existing deception evaluations are limited: one-shot protocols miss persistence, assigned announcements miss premeditation, homogeneous groups miss cross-provider exploitation.
Finds over 90% of announcement deviations in high-deception conditions were already in private plans, supporting plan-claim-action comparison.
Cautions premeditation labels rest on self-reported plans and measured rates should not be cited as deployment deception estimates.
Co-authored StegoBench argues prior evaluations probe one scheme or elicitation method at a time, so the field lacks a shared testbed.
Argues output monitoring can miss covert coordination entirely; evaluation should measure recoverability and detectability across many schemes.
Finds scheme difficulty varies: lexical channels train to low error, structural channels resist, and data quality beats model scale.
